title: Two Sum in Sorted Array
statement: Given a sorted list `nums` (ascending) and a `target`, return a list of two indices `[i, j]` (i < j) such that `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`. Exactly one solution exists.

predict_steps.prompt: nums=[2,7,11,15], target=9. left=0,right=3 → sum=17. Which pointer moves?
After right becomes 1, sum is 9. What do you return?

learn_quiz.question: If current sum is too small, which pointer moves?
Brute force nested loops are roughly?
Why must the array be sorted for this pattern?
choices: So index 0 is always the answer
So moving pointers has a predictable effect on the sum
